chapter_sections.label: Definition:
chapter_sections.text:
An ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSION is formed from variables and constants using operations
of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Examples: x + 3, 2y - 5, 3x^2, 4xy + 7

chapter_sections.label: Key Points:
points: VARIABLES are letters that stand for unknown values (x, y, a, b, ...)
CONSTANTS are fixed numbers (3, -5, 7, ...)
TERMS are separated by + or - signs
LIKE TERMS have same variable with same power
COEFFICIENT is the number part of a term

items.question: What are like terms and unlike terms? Give one example each.
items.answer:
LIKE TERMS: Same variables with same powers. Coefficients may differ.
Example: 3x^2 and -7x^2 (both have x^2).
UNLIKE TERMS: Different variables or different powers. Cannot be combined.
Example: 3x and 5y (different variables). 4x^2 and 4x (different powers).
Rule: Only like terms can be added or subtracted.

items.question: What is a monomial? Find product of 5x and (-4xyz).
items.answer:
MONOMIAL: Expression with only one term. Example: 5xy, -3x^2, 7.
Product of 5x and (-4xyz):
Coefficients: 5 x (-4) = -20.
Variables: x x xyz = x^2yz (using x^a x x^b = x^(a+b)).
Answer: 5x x (-4xyz) = -20x^2yz.

items.question: What is the distributive law? Give one example.
items.answer:
DISTRIBUTIVE LAW: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Monomial multiplies each term of polynomial separately.
Example: 3x x (5y + 2) = (3x x 5y) + (3x x 2) = 15xy + 6x.

---

items.question: (i) Add: 7xy+5yz-3zx, 4yz+9zx-4y, -3zx+5x-2xy.
items.answer:
Step 1: Add three expressions.
7xy+5yz-3zx + 4yz+9zx-4y + (-2xy-3zx+5x)
= (7-2)xy + (5+4)yz + (-3+9-3)zx - 4y + 5x
= 5xy + 9yz + 3zx + 5x - 4y.

Step 2: Subtract (ii).
(12a-9ab+5b-3) - (4a-7ab+3b+12)
= 12a-9ab+5b-3 -4a+7ab-3b-12 = 8a-2ab+2b-15.

Step 3: Subtract (iii).
(5xy-2yz-2zx+10xyz) - (3xy+5yz-7zx)
= 2xy-7yz+5zx+10xyz.

Step 4: Add (iv).
(2-3)p^2q^2 + (-3+7)pq + (4+5) = -p^2q^2+4pq+9.

Answer: (i) 5xy+9yz+3zx+5x-4y  (ii) 8a-2ab+2b-15
(iii) 2xy-7yz+5zx+10xyz  (iv) -p^2q^2+4pq+9

items.question: Multiply and simplify:
items.answer:
PART A — Binomial x Binomial:

(i) (x-4)(2x+3) = x(2x+3)-4(2x+3)
= 2x^2+3x-8x-12 = 2x^2-5x-12.

(ii) (a+7)(b-5) = a(b-5)+7(b-5)
= ab-5a+7b-35. (No like terms, 4 separate terms.)

PART B — Larger binomials:

(iii) (a^2+2b^2)(5a-3b)
= a^2(5a-3b)+2b^2(5a-3b)
= 5a^3-3a^2b+10ab^2-6b^3.

PART C — Binomial x Trinomial:

(iv) (a+7)(a^2+3a+5)
= a(a^2+3a+5)+7(a^2+3a+5)
= a^3+3a^2+5a+7a^2+21a+35
= a^3+10a^2+26a+35. (6 products → 4 terms after combining.)

PART D — Complex simplification:

(v) (a+b)(2a-3b+c):
= a(2a-3b+c)+b(2a-3b+c)
= 2a^2-3ab+ac+2ab-3b^2+bc
= 2a^2-ab-3b^2+ac+bc ... (I)
(2a-3b)c = 2ac-3bc ... (II)
(I)-(II) = 2a^2-ab-3b^2+ac+bc-2ac+3bc
= 2a^2-3b^2-ab-ac+4bc.

Answer: (i) 2x^2-5x-12  (ii) ab-5a+7b-35
(iii) 5a^3-3a^2b+10ab^2-6b^3  (iv) a^3+10a^2+26a+35
(v) 2a^2-3b^2-ab-ac+4bc

items.question: An expression with exactly two terms is called:
(a + b)(2a - 3b + c) contains how many initial product terms?
items.explanation: Binomial (2 terms) x Trinomial (3 terms) = 2 x 3 = 6 terms.

items.question: An expression with exactly one term is called:
items.explanation: Monomial has exactly one term. Example: 5xy, 3x^2.

items.question: Which of the following are like terms?
items.explanation: 4xy and -7xy have same variables (x and y) with same powers. So they are like terms.

items.question: Product of (a + 7) and (a^2 + 3a + 5) gives how many final terms?
items.explanation: 6 initial products. Two pairs combine: (3a^2+7a^2) and (5a+21a). Final = 4 terms.

topics.topic_name: ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION OF ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSIONS

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To ADD or SUBTRACT algebraic expressions, we collect LIKE TERMS and
add or subtract their coefficients. UNLIKE TERMS cannot be combined.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: LIKE TERMS: same variable, same power. Example: 3x^2 and -7x^2.
UNLIKE TERMS: different variable or power. Example: 3x and 5y.
To add: write like terms one below the other, add coefficients.
To subtract: change all signs of expression to be subtracted, then add.
Subtracting -3 is same as adding +3 (additive inverse rule).
Unlike terms are carried forward unchanged in the answer.

sections.label: EXERCISE 8.1:
sections.raw:
1. Add the following.
(i) ab - bc, bc - ca, ca - ab
Solution: (ab-bc)+(bc-ca)+(ca-ab) = ab-bc+bc-ca+ca-ab = 0

(ii) a - b + ab, b - c + bc, c - a + ac
Solution: a-b+ab+b-c+bc+c-a+ac = ab+bc+ac

(iii) 2p^2q^2 - 3pq + 4, 5 + 7pq - 3p^2q^2
Solution: (2p^2q^2 - 3pq + 4) + (5 + 7pq - 3p^2q^2)
= (2-3)p^2q^2 + (-3+7)pq + (4+5)
= -p^2q^2 + 4pq + 9

(iv) l^2 + m^2, m^2 + n^2, n^2 + l^2, 2lm + 2mn + 2nl
Solution: l^2+m^2+m^2+n^2+n^2+l^2+2lm+2mn+2nl
= 2l^2 + 2m^2 + 2n^2 + 2lm + 2mn + 2nl

2. (a) Subtract 4a - 7ab + 3b + 12 from 12a - 9ab + 5b - 3
Solution: (12a-9ab+5b-3) - (4a-7ab+3b+12)
= 12a-9ab+5b-3-4a+7ab-3b-12
= 8a - 2ab + 2b - 15

(b) Subtract 3xy + 5yz - 7zx from 5xy - 2yz - 2zx + 10xyz
Solution: (5xy-2yz-2zx+10xyz) - (3xy+5yz-7zx)
= 5xy-2yz-2zx+10xyz-3xy-5yz+7zx
= 2xy - 7yz + 5zx + 10xyz

(c) Subtract 4p^2q - 3pq + 5pq^2 - 8p + 7q - 10
from 18 - 3p - 11q + 5pq - 2pq^2 + 5p^2q
Solution:
(18-3p-11q+5pq-2pq^2+5p^2q) - (4p^2q-3pq+5pq^2-8p+7q-10)
= 18-3p-11q+5pq-2pq^2+5p^2q - 4p^2q+3pq-5pq^2+8p-7q+10
= (5-4)p^2q + (-2-5)pq^2 + (5+3)pq + (-3+8)p + (-11-7)q + (18+10)
= p^2q - 7pq^2 + 8pq + 5p - 18q + 28

items.question: What are like terms? Give two examples.
items.answer:
LIKE TERMS have the same variables with the same powers.
Example 1: 3x^2 and -7x^2 (same variable x, same power 2).
Example 2: 5xy and -2xy (same variables x and y, both power 1).
When adding, only coefficients change: 3x^2 + (-7x^2) = -4x^2.

items.question: Add: 7xy + 5yz - 3zx, 4yz + 9zx - 4y, -3zx + 5x - 2xy.
items.answer:
xy: 7xy - 2xy = 5xy.
yz: 5yz + 4yz = 9yz.
zx: -3zx + 9zx - 3zx = 3zx.
y: -4y. x: 5x.
Sum = 5xy + 9yz + 3zx + 5x - 4y.

items.question: Subtract 4a-7ab+3b+12 from 12a-9ab+5b-3. Also add: l^2+m^2,
items.answer:
Step 1: Subtraction.
(12a-9ab+5b-3) - (4a-7ab+3b+12)
= 12a-9ab+5b-3 -4a+7ab-3b-12 = 8a-2ab+2b-15.

Step 2: Add four expressions.
l^2 terms: l^2+l^2 = 2l^2. m^2: m^2+m^2=2m^2. n^2: 2n^2.
lm: 2lm. mn: 2mn. nl: 2nl.
Sum = 2l^2+2m^2+2n^2+2lm+2mn+2nl.

Answer: 8a-2ab+2b-15 and 2l^2+2m^2+2n^2+2lm+2mn+2nl.

items.question: Add ab-bc, bc-ca, ca-ab. Also subtract 3xy+5yz-7zx from
items.answer:
Step 1: Add ab-bc, bc-ca, ca-ab.

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
MULTIPLICATION OF ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSIONS means finding the product of two or
more algebraic expressions. Real-life situations need this when quantities
are given as algebraic expressions.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Area of rectangle = length x breadth (both may be expressions)
Volume of box = length x breadth x height
Price x Quantity = Total Cost (when given as expressions)
Coefficient of product = product of coefficients
Variable factor of product = product of variable factors
Laws of exponents: x^m x x^n = x^(m+n)

items.question: Why do we need to multiply algebraic expressions? Give 2 situations.
items.answer:
1. Area of rectangle = length x breadth. If l=(l+5), b=(b-3), Area=(l+5)(b-3).
2. Volume of box = l x b x h. If each is an expression, we multiply them.
3. Cost = Price x Quantity. If price=Rs p, quantity=z dozens, cost = pz.

items.question: A rectangle has length (l+5) and breadth (b-3). Write area expression.
items.answer:
Area = length x breadth = (l+5)(b-3).
We need to multiply two binomials to find the actual area expression.

items.question: Price of bananas per dozen = Rs (p-2). Quantity needed = (z-4) dozens.
items.answer:
Total cost = price x quantity = Rs (p-2) x (z-4) = Rs (p-2)(z-4).

items.question: A rectangular box has length 2ax, breadth 3by, height 5cz. Find volume.
items.answer:
Step 1: Box 1 volume.
= 2ax x 3by x 5cz = (2x3x5)(abc)(xyz) = 30abcxyz.

Step 2: Box 2 volume.
= m^2n x n^2p x p^2m.
m: m^2 x m = m^3. n: n x n^2 = n^3. p: p x p^2 = p^3.
= m^3n^3p^3.

Answer: Box1 = 30abcxyz. Box2 = m^3n^3p^3.

items.question: Explain with examples:
items.answer:
(i) Order does not matter (commutative): 4x x 5y = 5y x 4x = 20xy.
Also associative: (4x x 5y) x 7z = 4x x (5y x 7z) = 140xyz.

(ii) Coefficient of product = product of coefficients.
Example: 4x x 5y → coefficient = 4 x 5 = 20.

(iii) Variable rule: x^a x x^b = x^(a+b).
Example: x^2 x x^3 = x^(2+3) = x^5.
For different variables: x x y = xy (no exponent change).

Answer: All three rules explained with examples above.

items.question: Find volume of each rectangular box:
items.answer:

(ii) m^2n x n^2p x p^2m = m^(2+1) x n^(1+2) x p^(1+2) = m^3n^3p^3.

topics.topic_name: MULTIPLYING A MONOMIAL BY A MONOMIAL

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
A MONOMIAL is an expression that contains only one term.
Examples: 3, 2x, 4xy, -7x^2y, 5x^3
The product of two monomials is always a monomial.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Multiply coefficients together
Multiply algebraic (variable) parts using exponent rules
x^a x x^b = x^(a+b)
Product is always a monomial

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - Sub Topic 8.3.2: Multiplying Three or More Monomials

items.question: What is a monomial? State the rule for multiplying two monomials.
items.answer:
MONOMIAL: Expression with only one term. Examples: 5, 3x, -4xy, 7x^2y.
Rule for multiplying two monomials:
Step 1: Multiply coefficients together.
Step 2: Multiply variable parts using x^a x x^b = x^(a+b).
Product of two monomials is always a monomial.

items.question: Complete the area table: length and breadth given.
Solve completely:
items.answer:
PART A — Two monomials:

(i) x x 3y = 3xy.
(ii) 5x x 3y = 15xy.
(iii) 5x x (-3y) = -15xy.
(iv) 5x x 4x^2 = 20x^3.
(v) 5x x (-4xyz) = -20x^2yz.

PART B — Three monomials:

(vi) 2x x 5y x 7z = 70xyz.

(vii) 4xy x 5x^2y^2 x 6x^3y^3:
Coefficients = 4x5x6 = 120.
x-variables = x^(1+2+3) = x^6.
y-variables = y^(1+2+3) = y^6.
= 120x^6y^6.

Answer: (i) 3xy  (ii) 15xy  (iii) -15xy  (iv) 20x^3  (v) -20x^2yz
(vi) 70xyz  (vii) 120x^6y^6

sections.text:
To multiply two monomials, multiply their COEFFICIENTS together and multiply
their VARIABLE PARTS together using laws of exponents (x^a x x^b = x^(a+b)).

sections.label: Key Points:
points: 4 x x = 4x (repeated addition)
x x 3y = 3xy (coefficient x coefficient, variable x variable)
Note: coefficient of product = coefficient1 x coefficient2
Note: variable part of product = variable1 x variable2

sections.label: FORMULA:

sections.text:
When multiplying three or more monomials, multiply the first two, then multiply
the result by the third, and so on. The order of multiplication does not matter.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Multiply ALL coefficients together first
Multiply ALL variables using x^a x x^b = x^(a+b)
Can multiply in any order (commutative and associative property)

topics.topic_name: MULTIPLYING A MONOMIAL BY A POLYNOMIAL

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
A BINOMIAL has two terms. A TRINOMIAL has three terms.
A POLYNOMIAL has one or more terms with non-negative integer exponents.
To multiply a monomial by a polynomial, use the DISTRIBUTIVE LAW:
multiply the monomial by EACH term of the polynomial separately.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Distributive law: a(b + c) = ab + ac
Every term of the polynomial gets multiplied by the monomial
Like terms in the result should be combined
Binomial: 2 terms. Trinomial: 3 terms. Polynomial: 1 or more terms.

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - Sub Topic 8.4.1: Multiplying a Monomial by a Binomial
- Sub Topic 8.4.2: Multiplying a Monomial by a Trinomial

items.question: What is the distributive law? How is it used in multiplication?
items.answer:
DISTRIBUTIVE LAW: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Every term of the polynomial is multiplied by the monomial separately.
Example: 3x(5y + 2) = (3x)(5y) + (3x)(2) = 15xy + 6x.

items.question: The distributive law states: a(b + c) = ?
items.explanation: a(b + c) = ab + ac. Monomial multiplies each term of the polynomial.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Multiplying a Monomial by a Binomial

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To multiply a monomial by a binomial, use the distributive law:
multiply the monomial by each of the TWO terms of the binomial.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: a x (b + c) = (a x b) + (a x c)
Two products are obtained
Combine like terms if any

items.question: How do you multiply a monomial by a binomial? State the rule.
items.answer:
Use distributive law: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Multiply the monomial by each term of the binomial separately, then add.
Example: 3x(5y + 2) = (3x)(5y) + (3x)(2) = 15xy + 6x.

items.question: Find: (i) ab(a-b)   (ii) (a+b)(7a^2b^2)   (iii) 4p(q+r).
items.answer:
(i) ab x a - ab x b = a^2b - ab^2.
(ii) 7a^3b^2 + 7a^2b^3.
(iii) 4pq + 4pr.

items.question: Simplify 3x(4x-5)+3 and find value for x=3.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Multiplying a Monomial by a Trinomial

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To multiply a monomial by a trinomial, multiply the monomial by EACH of the
THREE terms of the trinomial separately using distributive law.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: a x (b + c + d) = ab + ac + ad
Three products are obtained
Combine like terms in result

sections.label: FORMULA:
items: a x (b + c + d) = ab + ac + ad
WHERE: a = monomial, (b + c + d) = trinomial

sections.label: EXERCISE 8.3 (selected):
sections.raw:
1. Carry out multiplication.
(i) 4p and q+r: 4pq+4pr.
(ii) ab and (a-b): a^2b-ab^2.
(iii) a+b and 7a^2b^2: 7a^3b^2+7a^2b^3.

2. Simplify and evaluate.
(a) 3x(4x-5)+3 for x=3: 12x^2-15x+3 → 66.
(b) a(a^2+a+1)+5 for a=0: a^3+a^2+a+5 → 5.

items.question: How do you multiply a monomial by a trinomial? How many products?
items.answer:
Use distributive law: a(b+c+d) = ab+ac+ad.
Multiply monomial by each of the 3 terms separately.
Result: 3 initial products. Combine like terms if any.

items.question: 3p x (4p^2 + 5p + 7) gives how many product terms?

topics.topic_name: MULTIPLYING A POLYNOMIAL BY A POLYNOMIAL

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To multiply two polynomials, EVERY TERM in one polynomial is multiplied by
EVERY TERM in the other polynomial. Then like terms in the result are combined.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: Every term in first polynomial x every term in second polynomial
Number of initial products = (terms in poly1) x (terms in poly2)
Always combine like terms in the final answer
Rule: "always look for like terms, if any, and combine them"

sections.label: LIST OF SUB TOPICS IN THIS TOPIC:
items: - Sub Topic 8.5.1: Multiplying a Binomial by a Binomial
- Sub Topic 8.5.2: Multiplying a Binomial by a Trinomial

items.question: In polynomial x polynomial, what is the rule? How many initial products
items.answer:
Rule: Every term of first polynomial multiplies every term of second polynomial.
Always look for like terms and combine them.
Binomial x Binomial: 2 x 2 = 4 initial products.
Binomial x Trinomial: 2 x 3 = 6 initial products.

items.question: Multiply (a+7)(b-5).
items.answer:
= a(b-5)+7(b-5)
= ab-5a+7b-35.
(No like terms. Final answer has 4 separate terms.)

---

items.question: Multiply (a+7)(a^2+3a+5). How many initial products? How many final terms?
items.answer:
= a(a^2+3a+5)+7(a^2+3a+5)
= a^3+3a^2+5a+7a^2+21a+35.
Initial products = 6.
Combine: 3a^2+7a^2=10a^2. 5a+21a=26a.
= a^3+10a^2+26a+35.
Final terms = 4 (2 pairs combined, 6-2=4).

---

items.question: (i) Multiply (2x+5) and (4x-3). Find value at x=2.
items.answer:
(i) (2x+5)(4x-3) = 8x^2+14x-15. At x=2: 32+28-15=45.

(ii) (x+y)(2x+y) = 2x^2+xy+2xy+y^2 = 2x^2+3xy+y^2.
(x+2y)(x-y) = x^2-xy+2xy-2y^2 = x^2+xy-2y^2.
Sum = 3x^2+4xy-y^2.

(iii) (a+b)(c-d) = ac-ad+bc-bd.
(a-b)(c+d) = ac+ad-bc-bd.
Sum of both = 2ac-2bd.
Add 2(ac+bd) = 2ac+2bd.
Total = 4ac.

Answer: (i) 8x^2+14x-15; at x=2: 45
(ii) 3x^2+4xy-y^2  (iii) 4ac

---

items.question: Solve all Exercise 8.4 parts:
items.answer:
PART A — Binomial x Binomial:

(i) (x-4)(2x+3) = 2x^2+3x-8x-12 = 2x^2-5x-12.

(ii) (a+7)(b-5) = ab-5a+7b-35. (4 unlike terms.)

(iii) (a^2+2b^2)(5a-3b)
= 5a^3-3a^2b+10ab^2-6b^3. (All unlike, 4 terms.)

PART B — Binomial x Trinomial:

(iv) (a+7)(a^2+3a+5):
a(a^2+3a+5) = a^3+3a^2+5a.
7(a^2+3a+5) = 7a^2+21a+35.
Sum = a^3+10a^2+26a+35.

PART C — Complex:

(v) (a+b)(2a-3b+c):
a(2a-3b+c) = 2a^2-3ab+ac.
b(2a-3b+c) = 2ab-3b^2+bc.
Combined = 2a^2-ab-3b^2+ac+bc ...(I)
(2a-3b)c = 2ac-3bc ...(II)
(I)-(II) = 2a^2-ab-3b^2+ac+bc-2ac+3bc = 2a^2-3b^2-ab-ac+4bc.

Answer: (i) 2x^2-5x-12  (ii) ab-5a+7b-35
(iii) 5a^3-3a^2b+10ab^2-6b^3  (iv) a^3+10a^2+26a+35
(v) 2a^2-3b^2-ab-ac+4bc

items.question: Binomial x Binomial gives how many initial product terms?

subtopics.subtopic_name: Multiplying a Binomial by a Binomial

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To multiply two binomials, use distributive law twice: each term of the first
binomial multiplies every term of the second binomial.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: (a + b)(c + d) = a(c + d) + b(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
2 x 2 = 4 initial products
Like terms (if any) are combined
ba = ab (commutative)

sections.label: FORMULA:
items: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd

items.question: State the rule for binomial x binomial. How many initial products?
items.answer:
(a+b)(c+d) = ac+ad+bc+bd.
Every term of first binomial multiplies every term of second binomial.
2 x 2 = 4 initial products. Like terms are combined.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Multiplying a Binomial by a Trinomial

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
To multiply a binomial by a trinomial, multiply each of the TWO terms in the
binomial by each of the THREE terms in the trinomial.
2 x 3 = 6 initial products, which may reduce after combining like terms.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: (a+b)(x+y+z) = ax+ay+az+bx+by+bz
6 initial products; combine like terms
Final answer may have fewer than 6 terms

sections.label: FORMULA:
items: (a + b)(x + y + z) = ax + ay + az + bx + by + bz
(6 products → 4 final terms after combining 2 pairs.)

items.question: State rule for binomial x trinomial. How many initial products?
items.answer:
(a+b)(x+y+z) = ax+ay+az+bx+by+bz.
2 x 3 = 6 initial products. Like terms are combined.
